context: A uni student interviews a retired engineer at home
purpose: Teach: 直径/潜水艦/機体/マスメディア/外科/刑法/栄光/団塊

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間いただきありがとうございます。広志さんは団塊世代を代表する技術者として、長くご活躍されてきたんですよね。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. Hiroshi-san, you've had a long career as an engineer representing the baby boomer generation, haven't you?
lines.style: Polite student opening an interview with respectful, slightly nervous formality.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いやいや、代表だなんて大げさだよ。まあ、若い頃は潜水艦の部品設計を任されていてね、責任は重かったな。
lines.en: No no, calling me a representative is an exaggeration. Well, when I was young, I was put in charge of designing submarine parts, so the responsibility was heavy.
lines.style: Humble elder deflecting praise, then warming up with quiet pride about past work.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 潜水艦ですか。すごいですね。設計といっても、例えばどのくらいのスケールのものなんですか?
lines.en: Submarines? That's incredible. When you say design, what kind of scale are we talking about?
lines.style: Curious student probing deeper with genuine surprise and follow-up question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: バルブ一つとっても直径が三十センチを超えるものもあってね。その後は航空会社に移って、旅客機の機体の強度計算もやったよ。
lines.en: Even a single valve could exceed thirty centimeters in diameter. After that, I moved to an aviation company and worked on strength calculations for aircraft fuselages.
lines.style: Detailed reminiscence with concrete numbers, casual storytelling tone of an experienced elder.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 機体の設計まで。当時はマスメディアでもよく取り上げられた分野ですよね。技術者が栄光の時代と呼ばれていた頃ですか?
lines.en: Even aircraft design. That was a field heavily covered by mass media at the time, right? Was it during what's called the golden age of engineers?
lines.style: Student connecting dots with academic framing, slightly leading question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 栄光なんてものじゃないさ。事故が一つあれば刑法で問われることもある世界だ。同期には外科医になった奴もいたが、命を扱う重さは似ていたかもしれん。
lines.en: It wasn't anything as grand as glory. One accident, and you could be questioned under criminal law. One of my classmates became a surgeon, and the weight of handling lives was probably similar.
lines.style: Sobering elder reflection cutting through romanticism, drawing thoughtful comparison.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 刑法のリスクまで…。そこまでの重圧の中で、何が広志さんを支えていたんでしょうか?
lines.en: Even criminal law risks... Under that kind of pressure, what was it that supported you, Hiroshi-san?
lines.style: Student lowering voice, moved by the gravity, asking a more personal question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 結局は家族と、同じ志を持つ仲間だな。君も研究を続けるなら、肩書きより人を大事にしなさい。それだけは覚えておくといい。
lines.en: In the end, it was family and colleagues who shared the same aspirations. If you continue your research, value people over titles. Just remember that much.
lines.style: Warm closing advice from elder to student, gentle but firm wisdom.
